text:
Maria (PM): Quick sync — the launch telemetry has two things we need to decide on for the next 2-week sprint: embeddings error spike (seen in 2.1% of requests, several customer tickets) and a Console UX polish request. Also a backlog ask for a per-route caching toggle from support. I want a prioritized plan + owners by EOD so we can lock sprint scope.

Aj (Eng Lead): For embeddings, I dug into routing logs. Looks like a fallback path is being hit more often when KV cache entries expire. I think we can patch it without model changes — estimate 2-3d to root-cause + 1d for canary. Need Kevin to confirm infra side.

Kevin (SRE): Confirming, I see a 5m backlog spike around 03:14 UTC where batching latency climbed and some requests timed out. snippet: ```
2026-02-12T03:14:10Z batch_queue.size=147 latency_p50=120ms latency_p95=430ms
2026-02-12T03:14:30Z errors.count=12 route=embeddings-v1 fallback=true
```
This looks like transient pressure + fallback thrash. If Aj's patch can reduce fallback churn we should be good.

Sara (CS): Customer A (enterprise) opened a Sev2 for embeddings diverging. They're pushing for a fix in the next release — if we push to next sprint without a hotfix they'll escalate. Customer B also reported higher latency but lower severity.

Lena (Product Designer): Console polish is the column reorder bug in Saved Prompts — small, 1-2d. It would be nice for demo customers but lower severity.

Aj (Eng Lead): Proposed prioritization criteria: impact (customers+sev), dev cost (dev-days), rollback risk. Quick matrix: embeddings bug = High impact / 3-4d / Low rollback risk (patchable), caching toggle = Medium impact / 5d / Medium risk, UI reorder = Low impact / 1d / Low risk. My recommendation: hotfix lane for embeddings + canary, include UI tweak if we have spare capacity, defer caching toggle to next cycle or do as spike.

Maria (PM): I agree with Aj. Decision: 1) Hotfix for embeddings (JIRA ENG-4321) assigned to Aj, canary owned by Kevin. 2) Console reorder (JIRA UX-214) — Lena to own, schedule as filler. 3) Caching toggle — move to backlog grooming, do a 2d spike (JIRA ENG-4400) to size.

Aj (Eng Lead): I'll pick up ENG-4321. Plan: diagnose+fix (3d), test in staging (half day), canary 24h. If metrics look good, roll to prod.

Kevin (SRE): I'll own the canary. I'll add a temporary alert for fallback-rate and a dashboard tile for latency by route. Can start canary once PR is merged.

Sara (CS): Tagging customer A: I'll draft the mitigation note and ETA once we have the canary start time.

deploy-bot: Canary started for ENG-4321 on dedicated-pool-7 — canary: 10% traffic.

Aj (Eng Lead): Nice, thanks. Quick ask: can we also capture a small eval prompt set to validate semantic drift from the patch? 15-20 prompts should do.

Lena (Product Designer): I'll queue UX fix and pair with Aj if we get spare cycles.

Maria (PM): Action items summarized: 
- ENG-4321 (embeddings hotfix) — owner: Aj; canary owner: Kevin; ETA start: today
- UX-214 (Console reorder) — owner: Lena; schedule as filler
- ENG-4400 (caching toggle spike) — groom in backlog, target next sprint
- Sara to notify Customer A with interim mitigation
Please add to the sprint board and tag me on PRs. :thumbsup:

Aj (Eng Lead): Added to sprint board and linked PRs. Will post updates in #eng-runtime if anything unexpected shows up.

Kevin (SRE): Canary metrics look stable so far (1h): p50 down to baseline, fallback-rate improving. Will report at 24h.

Sara (CS): Thanks team — I'll send the customer note after Kevin confirms 24h checkpoint.

Maria (PM): Closing thread — sprint scope locked for these items. If anything else critical comes up we re-evaluate. Thanks everyone. :pray:
